note: CAMPING IS SEASONAL (area brochure, 12/2020): the campsites along Indian Creek are open September 15 to May 15; every other campsite on the area, the Hi Pointe spot included, is open only during firearms deer season. Six primitive spots are mapped. The Indian Creek camp is in the main tract off Highway 185: about 1.5 km of gravel road to a gravel turnaround in open bottomland woods a short walk from the creek. The Hi Pointe spot, 10 km east on Pelican Ridge Road, is a short gravel spur with a turnaround in oak-pine woods. The other four are unmarked spots in the woods beside roadside parking lots in the main tract. No facilities, and spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - six GIS points and six map symbols over two tracts, free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. NEW: the brochure limits camping to Sep 15-May 15 at Indian Creek and to firearms deer season everywhere else, including the pinned Hi Pointe spot - season conflict (manual year-round) and a pin move to the Indian Creek camp proposed. No horse camp. Phone matches.
flags: SEASON CONFLICT (season group is manual 'year_round: true', so this result does not touch it): the area brochure (12/2020, linked from the area page) says 'Camping is permitted only in designated areas. ... Campsites along Indian Creek are open September 15–May 15. Other campsites are open during firearms deer season.' The area page itself does not repeat this, but its Rule 140 block ends with a bare 'Camping is prohibited.' after the standard text - elsewhere a page artifact, here probably the stump of this seasonal rule. The page's 2026-27 firearms deer dates: November portion Nov 14-24, late youth Nov 27-29, late antlerless Dec 5-13, alternative methods Dec 26-Jan 5. So the stored pin (the Hi Pointe spot) is open to campers for only a few weeks a year, and nothing on the area is open May 16-Sep 14. QUESTION for AWH: set season to opens 09-15 / closes 05-15 with the note 'Indian Creek campsites; all other campsites open only during firearms deer season' (and move the pin, below)? As pinned today the honest season would be firearms deer season only. Caveat written at the head of the note meanwhile.

PIN MOVE PROPOSED (to the clear main camp, ~10.5 km): stored 38.08547,-90.88268 = GIS point 152, the single Hi Pointe spot (a ~45 m gravel spur with a small turnaround off Pelican Ridge Road, in woods; drive-in and fine for a 23-ft rig, but deer-season-only). The only camp with a real season is Indian Creek: GIS point 92 at 38.07064,-91.00136 lies on a gravel road that leaves the Indian Creek parking area (lot 1610, 38.06663,-90.99737; reached by ~1 km of gravel from Highway 185) and runs ~500 m north-west along the east bank to a gravel turnaround loop ~25 m across at about 38.07080,-91.00202, with one side spur on the way. Proposed pin: 38.07080,-91.00202 (the turnaround, seen clearly on the 0.18 m/px leaf-off frame). The road stays on the east bank - no creek crossing seen; no ford, 4WD or length wording on the page or brochure. elevation_meters would need re-reading there.

CLUSTERS: main tract five points - 92 Indian Creek (above); 154 at 38.07828,-90.99533 (map symbol beside the Highway 185 lot; under canopy, nothing visible); 153 at 38.08029,-90.95806 (north-east lot at the end of a gravel road, point in woods ~110 m from the lot); 155 at 38.09004,-91.02755 (beside the Route N lot, in woods); 156 at 38.06420,-90.98189 (by the southern lot off Highway 185, beside two small ponds and a food plot). Hi Pointe tract one point (152). The page: 'Visitors to the main area will find several primitive camping areas, six parking lots and five access roads. The Hi Pointe unit has a camping spot, three parking lots, and a two-acre fish pond.' No split proposed: each is a single small spot, and all but Indian Creek are deer-season-only. The Route F and Metcalf School tracts have no camping symbol.
HORSE CAMP: none - neither the page, the brochure nor the map labels any camp equestrian.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept either way): Hi Pointe's 2-acre pond is ~250 m from the spot through woods. At the Indian Creek turnaround the creek (a headwater stream ~8-10 m wide between gravel bars) is ~40 m west through bottomland timber with no open apron - not creekside.
PHONE: (636) 441-4554 on the area page and brochure matches.
